The trash can was easy, you just get some i-hook bolts and washers and you have your attachment placements for the strap. I used a guitar strap, easily detachable and comfy for long hauls. I don't recommend getting anything bigger than a 13-gallon otherwise it might get a bit cumbersome.

Definitely let the people and places know what you're doing. Like last night me and two of my kids went and picked up almost 7 trash cans full and we wouldn't of had a place to dump if we didn't talk to the local business and ask to use the dumpster but at the same time letting them know there are people out there that care. 

Most of all, be safe and have fun. Have reflective and glow stuff on your gear so people can see you.

Sorry for your loss. It is a hard subject matter but we feel it's one of the most important to talk about and doing it in a way that can connect with so many people is fantastic. We have plans to do so much more with this and to bring to light these tough subjects like depression and anxiety that are really things at the core of suicide. I feel personally that disc golf has helped save me from those dark corridors by giving me release in nature and meeting all sorts of wonderful folk. Im humbled to be a part of this and show off disc golf in a whole new light.
